amendments: Section 7, ADR-0015 row and 'Other defaults': 'no socket passing in v1' and 'State Store backends in v1' use the forbidden milestone name v1. Name a milestone or none. Also record the known SO_REUSEPORT limitations (connections queued on a closing listener are reset unless tcp_migrate_req is set; QUIC 4-tuples are rehashed on UDP 8443) and the chosen mitigation (CBPF steering through golang.org/x/sys/unix, or an explicit HTTP/3 limitation).

Section 7, ADR-0008 row: define the local token bucket without a Node count. It is an operator-declared per-Node ceiling, optionally derived from a Node count that Ruralz Control publishes. State the fail-open over-admission bound as N x per-Node ceiling.

Section 6, architecture summary: 'builds immutable content-addressed Bundles, records them as Revisions' contradicts section 2, where the Bundle is the source directory and the Revision is the content-addressed digest. Suggested wording: 'validates Bundles from Git and builds them into immutable content-addressed Revisions'. The summary also uses 'gateway nodes', which section 2 forbids, and lowercase 'last-known-good'. Use Node and Last-Known-Good.

Add a system-wide rule: at most one blocking State Store round trip per Policy on the request critical path. Post-response writes (cache store, usage settlement) are asynchronous, bounded and droppable. Without this rule, ADR-0014 usage settlement and Response Cache or Semantic Cache stores break the stated round-trip limit.

Section 7, ADR-0014 row: state whether a local token estimate MAY enforce a Token Budget mid-stream (in onChunk), or whether the tokenizer is strictly pre-admission. The system overview currently counts tokens in onChunk.

Section 2: add the canonical term 'active Revision' (the Revision a Node is serving), distinct from Last-Known-Good (the persisted boot Revision). 02-configuration-model.md line 686 conflates the two, while 01-system-overview.md separates them.

Section 3, Policy row: amend 'Precedence: Route over Gateway' to 'Route over Gateway within a slot; additive types stack; a Gateway Policy with overridable: false cannot be replaced or excluded', to match 02-configuration-model.md.
Section 2, Env vars row: state that RURALZ_STATE_STORE_URL is the fallback source for Gateway spec.stateStore.url, not a process setting like RURALZ_CONFIG, RURALZ_DATA_DIR and RURALZ_LOG_LEVEL.
Section 2, Error codes row: give a one-line meaning per area code (especially STS and RT) so documents choose areas consistently.

Section 2 or 7: state that the artifact a file-mode Node pulls from an OCI registry is a Revision produced by `ruralz bundle build` and published by `ruralz bundle push`, and that a Revision digest covers the rendered, per-Environment Bundle after merge and substitution (matches 02 'Canonical form and Revision').

Section 2 Cell row: define 'optional regional Control' (for example a Ruralz Control deployment with its own Control Store serving one Region's Clusters, and its relationship to the primary Ruralz Control), or mark it as an Open question owned by 04/11.

Section 6 and vision P3: reword 'at most one bounded round trip per Policy' to 'at most one blocking State Store round trip per Policy before the response is committed; post-commit writes are asynchronous and bounded', so Response Cache and Quota settlement do not violate a binding principle.
Section 2 Rollout row: clarify that Rollout applies only when Ruralz Control delivers a Revision; file-mode change delivery is external to Ruralz and is not a Rollout.
Section 2, Revision row: `rev-<sha256:12>` is the display form only. The Control Stream, OCI pulls and Last-Known-Good verification carry and verify the full sha256 digest.

Section 2, Last-Known-Good row: distinguish the 'active Revision' (served while detached) from Last-Known-Good (the persisted boot Revision, promoted at the Cluster's promoted digest in Control mode). 'Config served during CP outage' is false for a Node detached mid-canary.

Section 2, Rollout row: add a `paused` state (entered on a failed gate with `autoRollback: false`, left by `ruralz rollout resume` or `rollback`), or state that pausing happens inside canary or progressing. This is needed to close OQ-system-overview-17.
Section 2, Control-plane persistence row: say whether Revision content and audit segments stored by digest outside the Raft log are part of the Control Store.
Section 3, Policy row: 'Route over Gateway within a slot; additive types stack; a Gateway Policy with overridable: false cannot be replaced or excluded' (carried over).
Section 2 Rollout row: add a `paused` state, or state that a pause without `autoRollback` is represented within `progressing` (see OQ-system-overview-17).
Section 2 Revision row: 'content-addressed digest of a Bundle rendered for one Environment' (as proposed by Configuration model, Canonical form and Revision).
Section 2 Cell row: point 'optional regional Control' to OQ-system-overview-16 until its role (own Control Store, Raft non-voter or relay) is decided.

Section 2, Control Stream row: state that Nodes always dial ruralz-control on 8091 and Revisions flow down that Node-initiated stream, because connection direction decides NAT and egress-only firewall compatibility and the three drafts disagreed on it.

Section 2, Last-Known-Good row: add the promotion rule that a Revision becomes Last-Known-Good when its Rollout reaches complete in Control mode and on activation in file mode, because promoting on activation lets a Revision that failed its canary gate become the boot configuration after a restart (OQ-system-overview-2).

Section 2, Rollout row: give each state a one-line meaning, in particular that any NACK or failed gate ends in rolled-back and failed means only that the revert itself could not finish, because the drafts assigned a canary NACK to different terminal states.

Section 7: add a row, backed by a new ADR, deciding whether Revisions and Plugin artifacts are signed, who signs them in file mode and Control mode, and whether Nodes verify by default, because every draft asserted or assumed signing that the foundation pack never decides (OQ-system-overview-3).

Section 2, Default ports row: add a default Raft peer port for ruralz-control, or state that Raft traffic is multiplexed over 8091, because the embedded Control Store needs peer traffic and the pack lists only 8090 and 8091 (OQ-system-overview-7).

Section 2, Revision row: say whether the digest covers the Bundle source or the Bundle rendered with one Environment overlay, because that decides whether Environments can share a Revision and what Drift detection compares (OQ-system-overview-14).
Section 7, ADR-0009 row: assign HTTP/3 on UDP 8443 a milestone tag, because the ports row reserves UDP 8443 but no milestone is given and component documents need one (OQ-system-overview-1).

Section 2, Default ports row: state that /readyz reports an active validated Revision, bound listeners and no drain, and does not fail when the Control Stream is lost, because failing readiness during a control-plane outage would pull every Node from load balancing at once.
Section 7: add the YAML 1.2 parser and the JSON Schema draft 2020-12 validator (custom keywords and source positions) as fixed technology choices owned by the tech stack document.

Section 2 (Revision row): define a Revision as the digest of a versioned canonical serialization (for example ruralz.canonical.v1) that pins schema and registry defaults, so identical digests imply identical behavior across Node versions.
Section 4: state that a Filter's failure mode in onChunk after response commit terminates the stream and in onLog only records telemetry, consistent with 'onLog cannot modify the response'.

Section 2 Revision row: 'content-addressed digest of a Bundle rendered for one Environment (canonical hub form after overlay merge and ${VAR} substitution)'. Section 6 summary: replace 'builds immutable content-addressed Bundles, records them as Revisions' with 'renders Bundles into immutable content-addressed Revisions'. Closes OQ-system-overview-14.
Section 3 preamble: each Policy type's spec.config schema is authored by its feature document and registered and published by 02-configuration-model (OQ-configuration-model-9).
Section 2/9: CRDs use apiVersion ruralz.io/v1alpha1 and translate losslessly to Bundle ruralz/v1alpha1, unless OQ-configuration-model-1 decides otherwise.

Section 5: replace 'multi-file merge in deterministic (lexical) order' with 'base files form a union read in lexical order; duplicate identity is an error; only overlays/<env>/ patch resources (strategic merge)'.
Section 3 Consumer row: if the secretRef alternative is kept, 'API keys stored hashed; a secretRef-held key is hashed by the Node at load'.
Section 8 glossary seed: add Filter class, slot and upstream leg.

Section 3 Policy row: amend 'Precedence: Route over Gateway' to 'Precedence is per slot: a Route Policy replaces a Gateway Policy in the same slot unless that Gateway Policy sets overridable: false; Policies in different slots stack; Upstream-scoped Policies apply to the upstream leg only'.

Section 3 introduction: state that 02-configuration-model.md owns the envelope, every kind's spec fields and the Policy type registry, while each Policy type's config schema is authored by its feature document and registered in 02-configuration-model.md (resolves OQ-configuration-model-9; also relax style-guide section 5 accordingly).

Section 2 Config unit row: record that Kubernetes CRDs use API group ruralz.io (apiVersion ruralz.io/v1alpha1) and translate losslessly to Bundle apiVersion ruralz/v1alpha1, pending OQ-configuration-model-1.
Section 2 Error codes row: record that the RZ-CFG-NNN registry (currently RZ-CFG-001..025) is owned by docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md.
Section 2 Revision row: 'content-addressed digest of a Bundle rendered for one Environment' (resolves OQ-system-overview-14, as proposed in the document).
Section 3 Consumer row: 'API keys (stored hashed; a secretRef-held key is hashed by the Node at load)' (OQ-configuration-model-14).
Section 2, Revision row: change the definition to "content-addressed digest of a Bundle rendered for one Environment" (resolves OQ-system-overview-14; 02 Canonical form and Revision).

Section 3, Consumer row: "Caller identity: API keys (stored hashed; a secretRef-held key is hashed by the Node at load and only the hash is kept in memory), JWT subject/claim binding, OAuth client; tier, quotas, tags" (OQ-configuration-model-14).

Section 3 intro: state that each Policy type's spec.config schema is authored by its feature document and registered and published by docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md, which fixes the fields it uses (OQ-configuration-model-9).

Section 3, Policy row: replace 'Precedence: Route over Gateway' with slot-based precedence (a Route Policy replaces a Gateway Policy only in the same `slot`, all client-authentication types share slot `auth`, additive types such as `ratelimit` and `quota` stack by default) plus the `overridable: false` guardrail, because per-type override cannot let `auth.api-key` replace `auth.jwt` and unguarded override lets any Route drop platform authentication or abuse limits.

Section 3, Policy row: list the dotted type identifiers from the configuration-model registry (`auth.jwt`, `auth.api-key`, `authz.cel`, `transform.request`, `ai.token-budget`, `ai.semantic-cache`, `plugin`, ...) under the existing families, because the drafts drifted into `rateLimit`, `apiKey` and `tokenBudget` and later documents need one registry to cite.

Section 3, introduction: state that 02-configuration-model.md owns every kind's field schema except each Policy type's `spec.config`, which its feature document authors and 02-configuration-model.md registers and publishes, because one document cannot own the configuration of every Filter and the current wording makes feature documents' config fields 'invented' (OQ-configuration-model-9).

Section 3, Gateway row: add 'exactly one per Bundle, declared in ruralz.yaml', because allowing several Gateways forces Route-to-Gateway binding rules and leaves conflicting Gateway Policies unresolved.

Section 3, Scope column: define 'cluster' scope as 'delivered in a Bundle to the Nodes of every target Cluster' and state that `Environment` and `Cluster` are never part of a Bundle or its Revision digest, because one draft read 'cluster' as 'a Bundle configures exactly one Cluster', which contradicts Rollouts of one Revision to many Clusters.

Section 2, Revision row: define the digest as covering the Bundle rendered for one Environment (overlay and `${VAR}` values applied, schema defaults not materialized, hub form serialized as RFC 8785 canonical JSON), because Environments and tool versions must agree on digests and the system-overview panel asked the same question (OQ-system-overview-14).

Section 3, Environment row: change 'promotion path' to 'promotion path for source commits (each Environment renders its own Revision)', because overlays and Environment variables are inside the digest, so the same Revision can never be promoted unchanged, a contradiction all three drafts shared.

Section 6 summary: change 'builds immutable content-addressed Bundles, records them as Revisions' to 'renders Bundles into immutable content-addressed Revisions', because a Bundle is the source directory and the Revision is the built artifact under the Section 2 canonical names.

Section 7, ADR-0016 row: record that mirrored CRDs use the dotted API group `ruralz.io` (`ruralz.io/v1alpha1`), translated losslessly from the Bundle's `ruralz/v1alpha1`, or move Bundles to `ruralz.io/v1alpha1` at the freeze, because Kubernetes rejects a CRD group without a dot (blocking OQ-configuration-model-1).

Section 5 (ADR-0003): add that the loader rejects anchors, aliases, merge keys, custom tags, duplicate keys and non-UTF-8 or BOM input, and that overlays use Kubernetes strategic-merge semantics driven by schema list types, because plain YAML 1.2 allows alias-expansion denial of service and RFC 7386 overlays replace whole lists and produce noisy production diffs.

Section 3, Route row: keep `topic` matching only together with an event-ingress declaration on `Gateway` (for example an `eventSources` list, Planned (M4)), because `Gateway` listeners are HTTP-only and a Route cannot match topics that nothing ingests (OQ-configuration-model-11).
